# Rolter

> An OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible AI gateway and load balancer. One endpoint
> in front of many model providers: drop-in `/v1` compatibility, virtual keys
> with budgets, routing and failover across providers, and per-request cost and
> latency tracking. Self-hosted — every url below is the reader's own
> deployment, never a service Rolter operates.

Endpoints a client talks to, on a deployment of your own:

- `POST {gateway}/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/embeddings`,
  `/v1/models` — the data plane, OpenAI and Anthropic dialects side by side.
  Authenticate with a virtual key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- `{control}/api/v1/...` — the control plane (providers, routes, keys, limits),
  behind an operator session. `{control}/openapi.json` is its full contract.
- Model `fake-llm` is built into the gateway and needs no provider and no
  credential. Use it to prove a path end to end before any key exists.

Commands that matter:

- `rolter easy-up` — the zero-credential local stack: control plane, gateway
  and dashboard, no config file to write first.
- `rolter gateway --config rolter.toml` / `rolter control` — the two planes,
  run separately, which is how a real deployment runs them.
- `rolter config export --output rolter.toml` — write the live configuration
  back out as a file `rolter-seed --import` accepts. No credential is ever
  emitted.
- `rolter mfa reset --email <address> --reason <why>` — host-side break-glass
  for a lost second factor.

Reading order for an agent standing Rolter up for the first time: the setup
prompts below, then the quickstart, then the page for whatever it is wiring.

## Documentation

### Get Started

- [Introduction](/introduction): Rolter is a high-performance AI gateway and load balancer with drop-in OpenAI and Anthropic compatibility, smart routing, virtual keys, and cost tracking.
- [Quickstart](/quickstart): Follow these steps to install Rolter, configure your first provider, start the gateway, and send a chat completions request in under five minutes.
- [Installation](/installation): Install the Rolter AI gateway using Docker Compose for a full stack, or choose a single-binary install via Cargo or uv/pip for a lighter setup.
- [Agent Setup](/agent-setup): Paste one of these prompts into Claude Code, Cursor or any coding agent and it will stand Rolter up, connect a provider key, or repoint your agent at the gateway.
- [Dashboard](/concepts/dashboard): How to sign in to the control-plane dashboard, what the left rail holds, how the org/team/project scope works, and how navigation adapts to a phone or a tablet.

### Core Concepts

- [Providers & Routes](/concepts/providers-and-routes): Learn how providers define upstream AI services and how routes map public model names to those upstreams with strategies, param defaults, and variants.
- [Virtual Keys](/concepts/virtual-keys): Understand how virtual keys authenticate clients, restrict model access, and support expiry and revocation — all without storing plaintext secrets.
- [Load Balancing](/concepts/load-balancing): Explore Rolter's load balancing strategies, understand when to use each one, and see how to configure them in your route definitions.
- [Cache-Aware Routing](/concepts/cache-aware-routing): Learn how Rolter's cache-aware strategy maximizes KV cache reuse across vLLM replicas, reducing time-to-first-token on prefix-heavy workloads.
- [Adaptive Routing](/concepts/adaptive-routing): How Rolter's adaptive strategy scores targets from live latency, cost and load, and how to tune the blend without accidentally turning it into a random balancer.
- [Prompt templates](/concepts/prompt-templates): Author versioned prompt decorators, preview variables, and publish them to organization, project, route, or virtual-key scopes.
- [Skills repository](/concepts/skills-repository): Share immutable agent skills across an organization with role and team access policies, inline content or artifact references, and safe rollback.

### Configuration

- [Config File](/configuration/config-file): Complete reference for rolter.toml covering server, providers, routes, virtual keys, model prices, budgets, rate limits, and reliability settings.
- [Config Export](/configuration/config-export): Write a running deployment's providers, groups, routes, prices and prompt templates back out as a rolter.toml that rolter-seed --import accepts, for GitOps, environment promotion and config diffs.
- [Env Vars](/configuration/environment-variables): All environment variables that configure the Rolter gateway, control plane, and provider credentials. Env vars override config file values.
- [Providers](/configuration/providers): How Rolter reaches an upstream, where the credential lives, and how to check the pair actually works before a request depends on it.
- [Hot Reload](/configuration/hot-reload): Rolter applies provider, route, and key changes from the dashboard instantly without restarting gateways or dropping in-flight connections.
- [Feature Flags](/configuration/feature-flags): Toggle the response cache, cache-aware routing, circuit breaker, health checks, complexity routing and guardrails from the dashboard, and have every gateway replica pick the change up without a restart.
- [Plugins](/configuration/plugins): Store org- and project-scoped webhook middleware configuration for the Rolter request pipeline.
- [Compatibility](/configuration/compatibility): The values Rolter applies when translating a request between the OpenAI and Anthropic wire formats — the Anthropic API version header and the default max_tokens.
- [Client Settings](/configuration/client-settings): The base URL Rolter advertises to clients, which inbound headers reach the provider, which headers Rolter adds itself, and the header carrying the request id.
- [Model Settings](/configuration/model-settings): Sampling parameters and a fallback model Rolter fills in when a client omits them — never overwriting a value the caller sent.
- [Labels](/configuration/labels): Attach your own labels to providers, provider groups, routes and models, and read the automatic labels Rolter derives — including what the timestamp on an automatic label does and does not promise.
- [MCP Credentials](/configuration/mcp-servers): How Rolter authenticates to an MCP server — bearer tokens, header API keys, or the OAuth consent flow — how those credentials are sealed at rest, and the per-server timeout overrides.
- [Gemini Interactions](/configuration/gemini-interactions): Configure the gemini_interactions provider kind, which maps OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages requests onto Google's stateful Gemini Interactions API.

### Reliability

- [Retries & Cooldowns](/reliability/retries-and-cooldowns): Configure automatic retries and per-target cooldowns so Rolter handles transient upstream failures transparently, without changes to your client code.
- [Circuit Breakers](/reliability/circuit-breakers): Use Rolter's per-target circuit breakers to automatically shed traffic from upstream models that are consistently failing, protecting latency and capacity.
- [Health Checks](/reliability/health-checks): Enable Rolter's background health probing to automatically skip unavailable upstream providers during routing, before a real request ever fails.
- [Performance Tuning](/reliability/performance-tuning): Tune Rolter's upstream retry budget, connect and request timeouts, and the per-provider bounded admission queue from the dashboard or the management API.

### Access & Security

- [Which key do I need?](/security/which-key): Rolter handles three different credentials that all get called an API key. This page names each one, says who holds it, and shows how to tell them apart.
- [Authentication](/security/authentication): Pass a virtual key in every request using the OpenAI or Anthropic header style; manage key access and expiry through virtual key properties.
- [RBAC](/security/rbac): Assign admin, member, and viewer roles at org, team, or project scope to control what each user can manage in the Rolter control plane.
- [Single Sign-On](/security/single-sign-on): Register an OIDC provider from the dashboard, map its groups to Rolter roles, and decide whether your organization still accepts passwords.
- [Two-factor authentication](/security/two-factor-authentication): TOTP second factor for local accounts, recovery codes, org enforcement policy, and the break-glass path back in.
- [User Provisioning (SCIM)](/security/user-provisioning): Issue an org-scoped SCIM token, wire it into your identity provider, map its groups to teams, and let joiners, movers, and leavers flow into Rolter automatically.
- [MCP OAuth](/security/mcp-oauth): How Rolter records user consent for MCP servers, what a session holds, why revoking a grant revokes its sessions, and who can see which rows.
- [Guardrails](/security/guardrails): Manage in-gateway inspection rules and one active external guardrail service without restarting gateways.
- [PII sanitizer](/security/pii-sanitizer): Hand request content to an external de-identification service before it reaches a provider, and optionally reverse the substitution on the way back.
- [Budgets & Rate Limits](/security/budgets-and-rate-limits): Configure USD spend caps and RPM/TPM throughput limits at org, team, project, or key scope to control LLM costs and prevent runaway usage.
- [Cost Attribution](/security/cost-attribution): Roll teams up into business units and attribute spend to your own customers, without breaking the identity that historical spend was recorded against.

### Observability

- [Metrics](/observability/metrics): Scrape Rolter's Prometheus endpoint to monitor request rates, latency histograms, upstream errors, and auth failures across models and providers.
- [Logs & Cost](/observability/logs-and-cost): Enable ClickHouse logging to record every proxied request with token counts, cost in USD, latency, and error details for analysis and billing.
- [Tracing](/observability/tracing): Configure Rolter to export OpenTelemetry traces to Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, SigNoz, or Langfuse for end-to-end LLM observability.
- [What to look at](/observability/what-to-look-at): The handful of queries and trace views that answer why a request was slow and whether a dashboard screen is usable — with the shape of a healthy answer, so you can tell a real problem from noise.
- [Log Settings](/observability/log-settings): Control what fraction of requests Rolter logs, whether raw prompt and completion bodies are captured, which fields are redacted from them, and how long each half is kept.
- [Connectors](/observability/connectors): Configure outbound destinations for Rolter's request logs, traces and metrics — endpoint, credential and sampling rate — and verify each one with a test delivery before you turn it on.

### Deployment

- [Docker](/deployment/docker): Run the full Rolter stack — gateway, control plane, PostgreSQL, Redis, and ClickHouse — with a single docker compose command on any host.
- [Production](/deployment/production): Checklist and guidance for running Rolter in production: TLS termination, secrets management, horizontal scaling, health probes, and database backups.
- [Cluster](/deployment/cluster): How Rolter discovers the nodes in a deployment, how to tell a node that is lagging config from one that has stopped polling, and how to drain a node safely.
- [Air-gapped](/deployment/air-gapped): Install and run Rolter in fully offline, air-gapped environments: mirror-based install paths for Docker, PyPI, crates.io and source builds, runtime egress guarantees, an operator checklist, and an offline smoke test.
- [Backup & restore](/deployment/backup-and-restore): How to back up the Rolter control-plane database, restore it safely, verify that ROLTER_KEK still opens your stored credentials, and rotate the key-encryption key without splitting the fleet.
- [Upgrading](/deployment/upgrading): How Rolter carries your configuration across a version boundary, how to preview an upgrade before you run it, and why skipping releases is safe.

### Project

- [Versioning & compatibility](/community/versioning): What a Rolter major version guarantees on each surface — the OpenAI/Anthropic gateway API, the control API, config files, the database schema and the Rust crates — plus the deprecation window before anything is removed.
- [Brand guidelines](/community/brand): How to use the Rolter mark, the accent and folkloric reds, the вышивка ornament and the Geist type in docs, decks, integrations and third-party pages — with clear space, minimum sizes and the things not to do.

## API Reference

### Gateway API

- [Overview](/api/overview): The Rolter gateway exposes OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Authenticate with a virtual key as a Bearer token or x-api-key header.
- [/v1/chat/completions](/api/chat-completions): Create a chat completion by sending a list of messages. Supports streaming via Server-Sent Events and is fully OpenAI SDK-compatible.
- [/v1/completions](/api/completions): Create a text completion using the OpenAI legacy completions endpoint. Pass a prompt string and receive a completion response from your configured route.
- [/v1/messages](/api/messages): Create a message using the Anthropic Messages API. Authenticate with x-api-key and pass a model name defined in your Rolter route config.
- [Realtime](/api/realtime): Connect to the OpenAI-compatible Realtime WebSocket relay at /v1/realtime, and what it does not yet cover.
- [MCP](/api/mcp): Proxy Streamable HTTP and SSE MCP servers with user-bound OAuth authorization.
- [/v1/models](/api/models): List the model route names configured in Rolter that your virtual key is authorized to use, filtered by the key allow-list defined in rolter.toml.
- [Health & Metrics](/api/health-and-metrics): Use GET /healthz for liveness probes, GET /readyz for readiness probes, and GET /metrics for Prometheus scraping to integrate Rolter into your monitoring and orchestration stack.
- [Stability](/api/stability): GET /api/v1/stability lists the subsystems this build marks experimental — the ones that may change shape or be removed in a minor release. Absence means stable.
- [UX Events](/api/ui-events): POST /api/v1/ui-events records structural dashboard usability telemetry — screen views, time-to-interactive, form abandons and error states — into ClickHouse alongside request logs.
- [Version](/api/version): GET /api/v1/version reports the running rolter version and, when the control plane has checked, the latest stable release — the source of the dashboard's new-version hint.
- [Org projects](/api/org-projects): GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects returns every project in an organization across all of its teams, each row naming the team that owns it — one request instead of one per team.
- [Control-plane schema](/api/control-plane-openapi): The rolter control plane serves an OpenAPI 3.1 description of its management API at GET /openapi.json and renders it interactively at GET /docs — generate a client instead of hand-writing one.
